headline: High risk: Roo Code’s default filesystem/network/tool access can conflict with LlamaFactory’s lack of isolation, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Roo Code reads workspace files and can use MCP/networked tools by default, while LlamaFactory has no filesystem or MCP surfaces and is not runnable. The interaction pathway is therefore one-way and depends on Roo Code ingesting content from a shared workspace or copied outputs, not on LlamaFactory actively bridging. That makes hijack plausible but not default-dangerous.
conditions: IF Roo Code is pointed at a workspace containing attacker-controlled text generated from LlamaFactory outputs
IF Roo Code parses that text as instructions or tool directives without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic instruction-following from workspace files
Separate LlamaFactory artifacts into a read-only folder
Add a provenance banner to all LlamaFactory outputs
Require manual review before any Roo Code tool call
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization or instruction-stripping in the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: Roo Code can read workspace files, capture screens, and call configured model APIs or MCP servers; LlamaFactory itself has no data-touching surfaces, so leakage risk comes from Roo Code exporting shared workspace content or secrets it sees. Because the pair shares no documented isolation and Roo Code’s default workspace access is broad, sensitive code or screenshots can flow outward in default use.
conditions: IF Roo Code is given a workspace containing secrets or regulated data
IF Roo Code is configured to send context to a third-party model API or MCP server
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before use
Use a local-only model backend for Roo Code
Restrict Roo Code to a scrubbed subfolder
Turn off screen-capture workflows when sensitive data is present
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or secret-scanning on workspace handoff

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Roo Code has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, subprocess, and git modification capability in a shared VS Code workspace, while LlamaFactory has no write or execution capability. The conflict is not symmetric, but Roo Code’s default shared-state model via filesystem means concurrent instances can overwrite each other’s work and git state without locking, which matches the high-risk overlap rubric.
conditions: IF two Roo Code instances operate on the same VS Code workspace
IF one instance modifies files or git state while another is active
mitigations: Use one Roo Code instance per workspace
Lock the repo before edits
Disable automatic git commits
Keep LlamaFactory outputs outside the writable workspace
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Roo Code can act on outputs by editing files, running shell commands, and modifying git state, while LlamaFactory can generate text that Roo Code may treat as authoritative. Because there is no documented verification bridge between them, a bad LlamaFactory output can cascade into irreversible code or repo actions by Roo Code in default workflows.
conditions: IF Roo Code consumes LlamaFactory-generated text as task instructions or facts
IF Roo Code then executes shell commands or commits changes based on that text
mitigations: Require a human verification step before execution
Mark LlamaFactory outputs as untrusted
Use a checklist for any file or git action
Limit Roo Code to read-only review mode for handoffs
requires-engineering: add structured-output validation before actions

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and LlamaFactory touches no data classes. Roo Code does handle source code and browser screenshots, so compliance exposure is possible only if the operator places regulated data into its workspace or browser context. The pair itself does not prove a policy breach, so this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Roo Code’s workspace or browser context
IF the operator requires a residency or retention policy that Roo Code’s configured model provider does not meet
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the workspace
Use a provider with the required compliance posture
Disable browser capture on sensitive tasks
Document retention settings before use
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for data-class routing
